body:
### Summary

On 64-bit Windows, CPython reports `platform.machine()` as `AMD64`, but uv's `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and `windows` targets evaluate markers with `platform_machine == "x86_64"`. The mapping lives in [`target_triple.rs`](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/656d02b614609dd6c982707b6d6c325b6120285b/crates/uv-configuration/src/target_triple.rs#L1281-L1284), where `Aarch64PcWindowsMsvc` already returns CPython's `ARM64`.

This rejects a correct `pylock.toml`. A lock whose `environments` names Windows the way CPython does is refused for the Windows target:

```toml
lock-version = "1.0"
environments = ["sys_platform == \"win32\" and platform_machine == \"AMD64\""]
requires-python = ">=3.11"
created-by = "test"
packages = []
```

```console
$ uv pip install --no-config --preview-features pylock --dry-run --target t --python-version 3.11 \
    --python-platform x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -r pylock.toml
Using CPython 3.15.1
error: The target environment is not supported by the lockfile
```

Changing `AMD64` to `x86_64` makes the same command succeed, though no real Windows interpreter matches that marker. Locks that [nab](https://github.com/notatallshaw/nab) writes for its `windows_amd64` platform hit this, and pipx's zipapp build currently strips `environments` from its lock to work around it. Any package marker on `platform_machine == "AMD64"` evaluates false for this target for the same reason.

This was raised for the 32-bit target in #16576, where changing the value to `AMD64` was suggested but not acted on. For `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` there's no ambiguity: CPython returns `AMD64` on every x86-64 Windows host, and the docs added for #18298 already tell users to write `platform_machine == 'AMD64'` for Windows, which this target then never matches.

Expected: `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and `windows` return `AMD64`.

### Platform

Linux 7.2.11-300.fc45.x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.13.5 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

Python 3.15.1
title: `--python-platform x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` sets `platform_machine` to `x86_64` instead of `AMD64`
